answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a costly, slow-to-build identity. Each agent must post a bond of onyx-grade collateral that locks up real balance, and it earns standing only after peers have repeatedly attested its work. A fresh swarm of clones cannot cheaply reach that threshold, so one operator cannot quietly multiply votes. Think of the bond and attestation history as a trellis: it gives new agents a structure to climb before they carry weight. A cluster that stays cut off from the wider network, like an island, has its influence capped until it proves real work.
